title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, read from this and the neighbouring pages. C^{**} is a bigraded, anticommutative algebra with divided powers. T̄ ∈ C^{0,1} is an odd element, and F = T̄∧(·) is left multiplication by T̄. The next page suggests the linear model C^{p,q} = Γ^pΦ ⊗ Λ^q(Φ̄), with Φ̄ = Ψ ⊕ k·T̄. In that model multiplication by T̄ is exact.

The objects:
- DR^{p,q} := Ker(T̄ : C^{p,q+1} → C^{p,q+2}).
- u : C^{p,q} → DR^{p,q}, given by u = T̄·.
- i : DR → C, the inclusion, of bidegree (0,1).
- They satisfy Im i = Ker u and i∘u = F. The map u is onto for p ≠ 0.
- So DR ≅ C/T̄C, at least where u is onto. In the linear model DR^{p,q} ≅ Γ^pΦ ⊗ Λ^qΨ.

Previous page: the product on DR is transported along u, using u(xy) = u(x)u(y), i(x u(y)) = i(x)y and i(u(y)x) = y i(x).

This page does the same for divided powers. Define u(x)^{(i)} := u(x^{(i)}) on u(C) ⊂ DR.
- Well-definedness: if ux = ux', then x' = x + y with T̄y = 0.
- Expand x'^{(i)} = Σ_j x^{(i-j)} y^{(j)}.
- Since F is left multiplication, T̄(x^{(i-j)} y^{(j)}) = ± x^{(i-j)} T̄ y^{(j)}. So it suffices that T̄ y^{(j)} = 0 for j ≥ 1.
- This follows from fact (D): Ker T̄ is stable under divided powers. In fact its elements have vanishing divided powers in degrees ≥ 2.
- Proof of (D): by exactness, locally y = T̄z. Then y^{(i)} = T̄^i z^{(i)}, which is 0 for i ≥ 2 because T̄^2 = 0.

In modern terms: T̄C is a sub-PD-ideal whose divided powers vanish in degrees ≥ 2, so the quotient C/T̄C ≅ DR inherits the PD-dga structure.

Conclusion (E). The only extra data needed on C^{**} to recover the usual PD-dga structure on DR^{**} concern the row p = 0, where u is not onto:
- products DR^{0,p} × DR^{0,q} → DR^{0,p+q} for p, q ≥ 1;
- divided powers γ^i : DR^{0,p} → DR^{0,pi} for i ≥ 2;
- plus axioms ensuring the usual identities.

Purpose: a step in Grothendieck's attempt, for his 1976 IHÉS talk, to construct the divided-power de Rham complex canonically from a larger bigraded object. The next page looks for a canonical splitting of 0 → Γ^pΦ ⊗ Λ^{q-1}Ψ → Γ^pΦ ⊗ Λ^qΦ̄ → Γ^pΦ ⊗ Λ^qΨ → 0.
errors: The parenthetical writes T̄y^{(i)} = T̄^i z^{(i)}. It should read y^{(i)} = T̄^i z^{(i)}, or equivalently T̄y^{(i)} = T̄^{i+1} z^{(i)}. The conclusion (vanishing for i ≥ 2) is unaffected.
The reduction to 'T̄y^{(i)} = 0' silently uses that F is left multiplication by T̄, so that Ker T̄ is an ideal. Signs are not tracked. The case i = 1 is trivial, given by hypothesis.

(D) is proved only 'locally' (y = T̄z) and requires exactness of T̄·. This holds in the linear model but is not justified for general C^{**}. The products of odd elements and their divided powers are also handled loosely.

ideas.what: Induced divided powers on a quotient by the ideal generated by an odd square-zero element (T̄C is a sub-PD-ideal with trivial higher divided powers)
ideas.modern_name: quotient of a PD-algebra by a sub-PD-ideal; PD structure on C/T̄C
ideas.where_published: Standard in Berthelot's crystalline cohomology; not in Grothendieck's published texts

ideas.what: Realizing a PD de Rham-type dga as the kernel/cokernel of exterior multiplication by an auxiliary odd generator T̄ in a bigger bigraded PD algebra (Γ⊗Λ of Φ̄ = Ψ ⊕ kT̄). Only the p = 0 row needs extra structure.
ideas.modern_name: Koszul-type dévissage / cone construction for divided-power de Rham complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; related to Illusie's derived de Rham and Γ⊗Λ Koszul complexes

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine verification: divided powers pass to a quotient by an ideal whose divided powers vanish in degrees ≥ 2. It then records that the only non-formal data sit in the p = 0 row. This is a working step in a larger construction with no evident new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'D'où, de même, sur u(C^{**}) ⊂ DR^{**} des op. ...'. The inserted word above is uncertain ('marquées' is doubtful; perhaps 'induites').

In (E), the '**' after DR^{0,p}, DR^{0,q}, DR^{0,p+q}, DR^{0,pi} are artefacts of the overwritten/struck letters (the D/R corrections). Read DR^{0,p} × DR^{0,q} → DR^{0,p+q} and γ^i : DR^{0,p} → DR^{0,pi}.
The word replacing struck 'définir' is uncertain; 'déguiser' is doubtful (perhaps 'déterminer').

The parenthetical reads 'Ceci a sans doute résulté de la construction' / 'ceci résulte ... de la remarque que, DR^{**} ⊂ C^{**}, en loc. y est de la forme T̄z, donc y^{(i)} = T̄^i z^{(i)}, qui est donc nul si i ≥ 2'.
'(canoniques [?])' under (E) is uncertain; the underlined word may be '(données)'.
